newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares close lower on huge volumes.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares close lower on huge volumes.

text.p: * Telecom sheds most of Wednesday's gains on big turnover
* Fletcher Energy dives on negative drilling news
* Volumes huge in good two-way trading
Price movements at close

The New Zealand share market closed lower on Thursday on very strong turnover of more than NZ$100 million.
The NZSE40 Capital Index ended the day 3.90 points lower at 2,381.08, led down by a weak Telecom and a sharp fall in Fletcher Energy shares, partially balanced by firming pulp and paper stocks.
"Volume was huge at $103 million and that was a big day," Luke Koekoek of brokers J B Were said.
Telecom was a third of the volume at $34 million, but there was also good trading in Carter Holt Harvey, Fletcher Paper and Lion Nathan.
"Fletcher Energy did a huge dive because they came out with a drilling report which basically was pretty negative relating to Perdana Deep (in Brunei)," said Tim Snedden of ANZ Securities.
"We had the view the well was unlikely to produce anything significant anyway but there were still punters in the market that had other views and they got a bit burnt on the day."
He said Telecom, down eight cents, shed most of "a crazy run" on Wednesday.
The remainder were steady with relatively muted gains in the paper stocks given the 30 point rise in the S&P pulp and forest products index overnight on the back of proposed pulp price increases.

"The market is busy and the outlook for tomorrow is for a market that is well underpinned, but which has run into good two-way volume to the point where it has lost a lot of volatility," Snedden said.
